// Shared per-spec data setup. Each spec's beforeEach RESETS then SEEDS via the app's /__test__
// endpoint — this is Arrange, not Assert. Specs still ASSERT only through the UI (data-testid).
//
// FAIL LOUD: /__test__/reset and /__test__/seed are the Arrange for EVERY spec, so they are a hard
// precondition — if either does not return 2xx the data is not in the state the test assumes, and a
// silent failure would surface later as confusing, misattributed assertion failures on unrelated
// specs (e.g. leftover rows because reset could not clear an FK-referenced table). We throw here so
// the break is attributed to the seed contract, and so a developer running its own spec sees the
// broken endpoint immediately instead of shipping it.
import { request, type APIResponse } from '@playwright/test';

const BASE = process.env.BASE_URL ?? `http://localhost:${process.env.PORT ?? 3000}`;

async function must(res: Promise<APIResponse>, what: string): Promise<void> {
  const r = await res;
  if (!r.ok()) {
    const body = (await r.text().catch(() => '')).slice(0, 500);
    throw new Error(`seed contract broken: ${what} returned HTTP ${r.status()} — ${body}`);
  }
}

export async function resetAndSeed(fixture: unknown): Promise<void> {
  const api = await request.newContext({ baseURL: BASE });
  try {
    await must(api.post('/__test__/reset'), 'POST /__test__/reset');
    await must(api.post('/__test__/seed', { data: fixture }), 'POST /__test__/seed');
  } finally {
    await api.dispose();
  }
}

// Usage in a spec:
//   test.beforeEach(async () => { await resetAndSeed({ /* rows this spec needs */ }); });
-- Free-text notes kept against a record in the app. A note names what it is about by type and id
-- (only projects take notes so far) and is stamped with when it was written so the newest shows
-- first.
CREATE TABLE note (
    id          BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    target_type VARCHAR(20)              NOT NULL,
    target_id   BIGINT                   NOT NULL,
    text        VARCHAR(2000)            NOT NULL,
    created_at  TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT note_target_type_ck CHECK (target_type IN ('project'))
);

CREATE INDEX note_target_idx ON note (target_type, target_id, created_at);

// Shared per-spec data setup. Each spec's beforeEach RESETS then SEEDS via the app's /__test__
// endpoint — this is Arrange, not Assert. Specs still ASSERT only through the UI (data-testid).
//
// FAIL LOUD: /__test__/reset and /__test__/seed are the Arrange for EVERY spec, so they are a hard
// precondition — if either does not return 2xx the data is not in the state the test assumes, and a
// silent failure would surface later as confusing, misattributed assertion failures on unrelated
// specs (e.g. leftover rows because reset could not clear an FK-referenced table). We throw here so
// the break is attributed to the seed contract, and so a developer running its own spec sees the
// broken endpoint immediately instead of shipping it.
import { request, type APIResponse } from '@playwright/test';

const BASE = process.env.BASE_URL ?? `http://localhost:${process.env.PORT ?? 3000}`;

async function must(res: Promise<APIResponse>, what: string): Promise<void> {
  const r = await res;
  if (!r.ok()) {
    const body = (await r.text().catch(() => '')).slice(0, 500);
    throw new Error(`seed contract broken: ${what} returned HTTP ${r.status()} — ${body}`);
  }
}

export async function resetAndSeed(fixture: unknown): Promise<void> {
  const api = await request.newContext({ baseURL: BASE });
  try {
    await must(api.post('/__test__/reset'), 'POST /__test__/reset');
    await must(api.post('/__test__/seed', { data: fixture }), 'POST /__test__/seed');
  } finally {
    await api.dispose();
  }
}

// Usage in a spec:
//   test.beforeEach(async () => { await resetAndSeed({ /* rows this spec needs */ }); });
-- Free-text notes kept against a record in the app. A note names what it is about by type and id
-- (only projects take notes so far) and is stamped with when it was written so the newest shows
-- first.
CREATE TABLE note (
    id          BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    target_type VARCHAR(20)              NOT NULL,
    target_id   BIGINT                   NOT NULL,
    text        VARCHAR(2000)            NOT NULL,
    created_at  TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT note_target_type_ck CHECK (target_type IN ('project'))
);

CREATE INDEX note_target_idx ON note (target_type, target_id, created_at);

The client page now shows the client's notes as a timeline, newest first, with a form to add a note. `bin/e2e` builds the app and the acceptance test passes. I didn't click through the new form by hand, and nothing tests merging two clients with notes.

The request mentions an "OfficeFloor server", but the server here is a standard Spring Boot app (the package is just named `net.officefloor`). I built it the same way as the rest of the code.

**Database:** `V106__client_notes.sql` lets the existing `note` table take `'client'` as a target type, alongside `'project'` and `'invoice'`. There's no new table, so client notes use the same storage and newest-first ordering as job and invoice notes.

**Server:**
- **New endpoints:** `ClientNoteController` adds `GET` and `POST /api/clients/{clientId}/notes`. An unknown client gets a 404.
- **`NoteService`:** gained the matching list and create methods.
- **Merging clients:** notes now move to the kept client, like contact history does. Otherwise the merged-away client's notes would have been left pointing at a deleted client.
- **Test seeding:** the seed endpoint now accepts `clientNotes` entries (`id`, `clientId`, `text`, `date`), which the test uses to set up its data.

**Front end:** I extended the existing `Notes` component (`app-notes`) rather than writing a new one. It now takes an optional `clientId` and is placed on the client page after the contact history. On a client page the list's test IDs are `client-notes` and `client-note-list`. The rows keep the existing `note-row-{id}`, `note-text` and `note-at`, which is what the test looks for. No existing test ID was renamed or removed.

One change to an existing API: `projectId` on `Notes` used to be required and is now optional, so the same component can serve clients. The job and invoice pages still pass it and work as before.
